title: Client handshake & backpressure playbook for hosted API (wip)
content:
Overview:

This is a working playbook for the Hosted API client handshake and backpressure behavior. It focuses on the end-to-end ergonomics for SDK clients and server-side signals necessary to keep streaming latency low while avoiding overload in downstream tool integrations. Drafted for product + SDK + serving-runtime alignment; intended to feed into a final PRD and an SDK implementation spike.

Why this matters:
- Customers integrating streaming model responses plus tool calling see two failure modes: client-side stalls (UI hangs) and tool downstream overload (webhooks, third-party APIs).
- Naive retry/queueing in SDKs hides backpressure and leads to cascading SLO violations.
- We want a predictable, debuggable, and ergonomic handshake that lets apps choose graceful degradation policies (e.g., partial output vs. fail-fast).

Goals (measurable):
- Provide a minimal, language-agnostic handshake spec usable by SDKs within 2 weeks of doc finalization.
- Reduce incidents where client UI waits >5s for the next token due to server-side queueing by 50% on high-concurrency tenants (measured in rollout canary).
- Ensure tool-calling integrations expose clear retry/backoff cues; reduce downstream 429s by 60% for customers using automatic tool calling.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not decide exact token batching thresholds or kernel-level scheduling policies for the runtime. Those remain infra choices.
- Not a full security/compliance spec for private deployments (KMS/HSM interactions are out of scope).

User stories / examples:
- As an app engineer, I want the SDK to emit partial structured outputs quickly so my UI can show progress while downstream webhooks are invoked at controlled rates.
- As a platform engineer, I want server signals that let me throttle low-priority requests without affecting high-priority interactive sessions.

Design summary (high level):
1) Three-phase handshake for streaming requests (CONNECT -> STREAM -> TEARDOWN) with explicit backpressure signals.
   - CONNECT: client opens session; sends metadata (priority, idempotency key, tool-caller flag, preferred max in-flight tool calls). Server returns 200 + session token or 429 with Retry-After.
   - STREAM: actual token/structured-chunk frames flow. Frames can carry control flags (PAUSE, RESUME, PREFETCH_HINT, TOOL_CALL_REQUEST). Client can send a light keepalive/ack frame to indicate it is still processing.
   - TEARDOWN: client signals completion or server indicates early termination with failure cause.

2) Frame model (wire-level primitives we need to standardize in SDKs):
   - DATA(token_chunk | json_chunk | binary_chunk) — an incremental content frame.
   - CONTROL(backpressure_level | pause | resume | server_hint) — server asks client to slow or resume.
   - ACK(seq_id) — client acknowledges receipt up to seq_id; used for server GC and routing decisions.
   - TOOL_CALL_REQUEST(tool_id, call_id, payload_meta) — server asks client to invoke a tool; includes idempotency token and a suggested deadline.
   - TOOL_CALL_RESPONSE(call_id, status, trace_meta) — client returns invocation result back to server streaming path.

3) Backpressure semantics (policy):
   - Soft backpressure: server emits CONTROL(backpressure_level=n) with n in [0..10]. SDKs should surface this as an advisory API event so app can choose to pause UI streaming or show reduced fidelity. This does not terminate the session.
   - Hard backpressure: server returns DATA with CONTROL(pause) or closes stream with TEARDOWN(code=RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, hint=Retry-After). SDKs must surface to callers and optionally retry according to app policy.
   - Tool-call backpressure: tool calls are treated as a separate budget; server will send TOOL_CALL_REQUEST only while tool_budget > 0. If budget exhausted, server queues or turns down requests with TOOL_CALL_RESPONSE(status=queued or denied). SDKs must not issue duplicate tool calls without the server's idempotency token.

4) Structured output directives and partial JSON:
   - We will allow structured JSON blocks to be emitted incrementally. Each JSON block must include a schema_id (optional) and a completion marker (e.g., DATA({"__schema_id":"x","__partial":true, ...}) and final frame with __partial=false).
   - SDKs should provide a utility to assemble partial JSON frames and validate final output against a lightweight schema (schema can be a URL or short descriptor).

5) SDK ergonomics (recommended behavior):
   - Default runtime: single request -> auto-reassemble frames -> emit token events + structured events.
   - Provide two high-level APIs: "stream_consume" (push-based callbacks) and "stream_iter" (async iterator returned to callers). Both must expose an event stream for CONTROL frames and TOOL_CALL_REQUEST events.
   - Backpressure handling: expose an on_backpressure(level, suggested_action) hook. Default SDK behavior: if level >=7, pause UI streaming and buffer up to N tokens (configurable, default N=512 tokens); if buffer hits limit, signal TEARDOWN candidate to server (close with GRACEFUL_PAUSE) unless app overrides.
   - Tool calling ergonomics: SDK should offer an opt-in tool-calling adapter that implements guaranteed once semantics with ack tokens, automatic deadline enforcement, and transparent webhook fallback. Document recommended default timeouts per tool type (external HTTP call default 2s for interactive apps).

Examples (pseudo flows):
- Interactive chat with tool: client CONNECT(priority=10, tools_allowed=true, tool_budget=2) -> server STREAM sends text frames -> server emits TOOL_CALL_REQUEST(call_id=abc, payload_meta={...}) -> SDK emits on_tool_call(call_id,..) -> developer callback invokes tool HTTP webhook -> SDK returns TOOL_CALL_RESPONSE(call_id, status=200, trace_meta) -> server resumes streaming. Backpressure: server may set backpressure_level=6 while tool call pending; SDK shows spinner but continues to surface text frames.

Open implementation questions / trade-offs:
- ACK frequency: how often should SDK ack (every token vs every N tokens)? Trade-off between RTT overhead and server memory. Proposal: default ack every 50 tokens or on CONTROL frames.
- Wire protocol: do we extend existing SSE + jsonlines model or standardize a small WebSocket subprotocol? SSE is HTTP-friendly; WebSocket gives bi-directional low-latency control frames. Proposal: initial SDKs default to long-lived HTTP/2 streaming with a small bidirectional WebSocket option for advanced integrations.
- Tool-call reliability: do we require server to support fallback routing for tool calls if client offline? For Hosted API, server should queue short-lived tool calls (30s) and return queued status. For Private/Dedicated, allow opt-out.

Telemetry and observability signals to emit:
- session_open_latency, session_rejects_429_rate, avg_backpressure_level_by_tenant, tool_call_denied_rate, avg_tool_call_latency, partial_json_errors.

Developer docs and SDK surface plan (milestones):
- Week 0-1: finalize handshake frames and minimal wire mapping. SDK spike (JS + Python) to validate. (GH PR #1345)
- Week 2: implement control frame handling and on_backpressure hooks in reference SDKs.
- Week 3: roll feature behind runtime flag; run canary against 5 customers in hosted environment.

Risks and mitigation:
- Complexity in SDKs leading to developer confusion: mitigate by shipping a high-level "simple" API that hides control frames, with an advanced mode exposing raw events.
- Inconsistent tool-call semantics across Dedicated/Private: provide clear defaults and allow customers to opt into queuing semantics.

Unresolved questions (action items):
- Decide wire transport (SSE vs WebSocket) for GA. Owner: Riley Chen. Ticket: HOSTED-1012.
- Converge on default tool_call timeouts per category (http, db, short-run lambda). Owner: Miguel Torres. Ticket: HOSTED-1013.
- Agree on default ack frequency and buffer sizes. Owner: Aarti Shah. Ticket: HOSTED-1014.

Next steps:
- Run SDK spike, gather perf deltas and update playbook.
- Draft user-facing docs with examples for chat UI and webhook-based tool adapters.
- Prepare canary rollout checklist (observability dashboards + SLA guardrails).

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add quick sequence diagram for CONNECT/STREAM/TOOL_CALL flow.
- Add small reference implementation of partial JSON assembler in python client.
- Link to existing streaming SDK PRs and runtime feature flag docs.

Slack references: #hosted-api-streaming, #sdk-ergonomics
